references.text: Jacob also asked his household to give up their foreign gods and earrings, showing that jewelry could be used in idol worship.
The Israelites received gold jewelry from the Egyptians when they left Egypt, and this gold was later used for the golden calf.
The Lord commanded the Israelites to ask the Egyptians for silver and gold items, which were later misused for idol worship.
The Israelites took gold and silver jewelry with them from Egypt, and this gold was later used to make the golden calf.
Gideon also collected gold rings from the people and made an ephod that became a snare for Israel, just like Aaron's golden calf.
Hosea describes how Israel used their gold and silver for Baal worship, which recalls the golden calf in the wilderness.
Narrative context: Aaron's role as temporary leader (24:14) leads directly to his mistaken initiative in the golden calf incident (32:2).
Theological contrast: The true calf as a sin offering (Lev 9:2) stands in direct opposition to the golden calf as an idol (Exod 32:4).
